question: Cross-browser opt-in mechanism for install.sh: should the system-deps installation (npx playwright install-deps webkit firefox) be gated by an explicit --with-cross-browser CLI flag, triggered by the presence of webkit/firefox in .cloverleaf/config/ui-review.json, or run unconditionally? The flag approach avoids config-at-install-time coupling and is predictable in CI environments but requires callers to opt in and a README note; the config-driven approach is ergonomic long-term but requires consumer config to exist before installation. A spike should evaluate platform-detection reliability (apt-only graceful no-op), assess how downstream consumers invoke install.sh today, and produce a recommendation with a concrete flag name or config-key convention.
findings: Three findings inform the decision. (1) Current install.sh behavior: `npx playwright install chromium webkit firefox` already runs unconditionally (all three browser binaries downloaded, ~600–650 MB); on Linux, `npx playwright install-deps webkit` is called but `install-deps firefox` is not — this is the gap causing the CLV-28 incident. The fix scope is adding firefox to the install-deps call and gating it appropriately. (2) Platform-detection reliability: playwright-core's own dependency installer (`lib/server/registry/dependencies.js`) already handles non-apt platforms gracefully — on macOS/Windows it prints a warning (`Cannot install dependencies for <platform>!`) and returns immediately with no system changes (exit 0, no sudo prompt). This means no additional bash platform guard is strictly needed inside the flagged branch; install-deps is inherently a no-op outside Linux. (3) Bootstrap problem rules out config-driven detection: install.sh is invoked from inside the cloverleaf checkout, not from a consumer repo root. The consumer's `.cloverleaf/config/ui-review.json` (where `browsers` is set to include webkit/firefox) lives in the consumer project, which install.sh has no reliable path to at install time. The package-level default (`reference-impl/config/ui-review.json`) ships with `"browsers": ["chromium"]` only — cross-browser consumers are the minority opt-in case. Running install-deps unconditionally would add 50+ apt packages on every Linux install for users who never enable webkit/firefox, and a sudo prompt on first install is intrusive for chromium-only users. Downstream consumer invocation patterns (confirmed in README and examples/toy-repo) are `./install.sh` and `./install.sh --project`; no existing call site would break from adding an opt-in flag.
recommendation: Gate the system-deps step behind an explicit `--with-cross-browser` CLI flag. When `--with-cross-browser` is passed on Linux, run `npx playwright install-deps webkit firefox` (replacing the current unconditional `install-deps webkit` only call). When the flag is absent on Linux, preserve the current behavior: run only `npx playwright install-deps webkit`. On non-Linux platforms the install-deps call is a playwright-level no-op regardless of the flag, so no additional bash guard is needed inside the flagged branch. The browser binary download (`npx playwright install chromium webkit firefox`) remains unconditional as today. The RFC task for install.sh should: (a) parse `--with-cross-browser` from `"$@"` at the top of install.sh; (b) replace the current `npx playwright install-deps webkit` block with a conditional that runs `npx playwright install-deps webkit firefox` when the flag is set, or the existing `install-deps webkit` when not; (c) print an informational note when the flag is absent — e.g., `"(Pass --with-cross-browser to also install webkit/firefox system deps for cross-browser UI review)"`. README should note: pass `--with-cross-browser` when `.cloverleaf/config/ui-review.json` sets `browsers` to include `webkit` or `firefox`. The shell-mock regression test should assert that `install-deps webkit firefox` is invoked when the flag is present and that only `install-deps webkit` (not `install-deps firefox`) is invoked when the flag is absent.
